rationale: I read the full held EO 1624 text (sha 04a9c7cf..., ProQuest OCR, signed Taft 1912-10-15, [No. 1624]): it amends Schedule A, Subdivision VII, paragraph 4 of the Civil Service Rules (fourth-class postmaster exception) and directs that postmaster appointment regulations be amended to certification of three names (offices $500+) or inspector recommendation. Identity is consistent with the 1989 row and EO 10869's Sec. 2 citation 'Executive Order No. 1624 of October 15, 1912' (OCR 'Ì2'). I read the full FR text of EO 10869 (sha 5b19c7fc..., 25 FR 2073): Sec. 2 says the listed orders and regulations, including EO 1624, 'are hereby revoked' - unqualified, whole order, no savings clause or exception, and Sec. 1 supplies replacement rule text independently. EO 1624 has no own-term sunset. The amend-rule command and the directive were one-time/continuing rule text now superseded by the revocation; the 1989 'Amended by EO 1776' note and EO 1776/1778 amending the regulations are not endings and do not contradict it (amendment of the postmaster regulations earlier does not end EO 1624; no earlier whole-order ending found). Other cruden hits (Wikisource EO 209 footnote, EO 1625 nav) merely cite it. The 1989 'Revoked by EO 10869' row is only a corroborating lead. This supports a provisional NO (ended by express revocation), but approved stays false because the held original is not an acceptable original and pages are unconfirmed; no date asserted.
